chapter: Struttin' Time, chronology and Chicago singers
title: Cora Green, Bricktop and the Panama dancers
summary: Cora Green had an in-between voice, Brick talked her songs and danced; Hunter had to dance in Show Boat in front of the chorus.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: Cora Green was -- Cora Green was nice. She had an in between voice, between sweet and jazz. You know

what I mean? She had an in between voice. Everybody on that floor was a different type, had different type voices. Everybody on each one of the floors upstairs and downstairs had different type voices.

Now, Brick was more of an entraineur. She talked most of her songs. She never could sing. But, boy, could she dance a while! Brick could dance, you know. Yes, all of them could dance, the -- all of them, the five of them.
Well, I wouldn't say I could dance, no, a little bit, although when I did Showboat, I had to get out there in front of those girls that they had brought over from America and dance.
They brought those girls over from America, and I had to get out in front of them and dance at Drury Lane, so I -- maybe I wasn't too bad.
